title: strip_draft_on_submit.sql manually SETs updated_at, contradicting the migration header's stated trigger convention
evidence:
+UPDATE application_draft
+SET fields = '{}'::jsonb,
+    continue_token = NULL,
+    submitted_at = now(),
+    updated_at = now()
+WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
+  AND email = lower($2)
+RETURNING id::text;
detail: The migration header states updated_at "follows the repo's trigger convention (update_updated_at_column ...), not manual SETs", and the BEFORE UPDATE trigger makes this SET dead. The other five new draft queries (claim, clear, erase, mark, upsert) correctly omit it — strip is the lone outlier.
recommended_fix: Drop the `updated_at = now()` line from strip_draft_on_submit.sql and regenerate; the trigger stamps it.

title: handle_continue_link docstring's response contract omits the upsert-failure ok:false arm it documents nowhere
evidence:
+//// response carries NO send/cooldown state (ok:true on every claim outcome;
+//// ok:false only when the Resend call itself failed) — a flag would oracle
+//// the victim's draft/submission state to an empty-fields poller (N14,
+//// Perkins r2). Claim DB failures are 500.
...
+              case upserted {
+                Error(_) -> wisp.json_response(json_ok(False), 200)
detail: The round-3 no-oracle contract says ok:false "only when the Resend call itself failed", but a failed upsert also answers ok:false/200 (the abort-before-claim arm). Harmless behaviourally (upsert errors are state-independent), but the normative contract text is wrong in the file the round-3 fix touched.
recommended_fix: Amend the docstring: ok:false on upsert failure (aborted before claim) or Resend failure; claim DB failures remain 500.
